games.reason: The shared element, SORT1-target, cell-context, and phenotype evidence does not distinguish the chains. HNF4G has a nearby HepG2 ChIP-seq summit, so B is plausible, but HNF4A is much more highly expressed in the matched context (90.2 versus 5.8 TPM) and has direct, repeated HepG2 ChIP-seq support at the variant, including peaks whose nearest summit is 15 bp away. That makes A the better-supported TF candidate. Neither chain has evidence here establishing that the alt allele binds more strongly; the ChIP evidence supports occupancy, not allelic direction.

HNF4A is better supported: it is highly expressed in HepG2 and has a near-variant summit in the family-screen evidence, while independent ChIP-seq evidence reports multiple HNF4A peaks overlapping the variant in HepG2. HNF4G also has a nearby summit, but its reported expression is much lower. Neither chain’s cited evidence establishes that the alternate allele binds more; that shared direction remains unsupported.
